title: Localization of an internal finite basis with its specified scalar map
statement:
Let $C$ be a small site whose abelian sheaves carry the sheafified tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], let $t$ be a global section of $R$, and let $I$ be a finite set. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and restriction of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Suppose global sections $b_i$ of $T$ give an $R$-module isomorphism
$$q:R^{\oplus I}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}T,\qquad (a_i)\longmapsto\sum_i\varphi(a_i)b_i.$$
Let $j_R:R\to A$ and $j_T:T\to B$ be morphisms of commutative ring objects exhibiting localization at $t$ and $\varphi(t)$, respectively. Explicitly, $j_R(t)$ is invertible and every ring map $R\to D$ making $t$ invertible factors uniquely through $j_R$; impose the analogous condition on $j_T$ and $\varphi(t)$.

There is a unique ring map $\varphi_t:A\to B$ with $\varphi_tj_R=j_T\varphi$. There is an $A$-module isomorphism
$$q_t:A^{\oplus I}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_t}B,\qquad (a_i)\longmapsto\sum_i\varphi_t(a_i)j_T(b_i).$$
It satisfies $q_tj_R^{\oplus I}=j_Tq$ and is the unique $A$-linear map satisfying this equation. No injectivity of $\varphi$ or nonzero-divisor hypothesis on $t$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0EMC (lemma-simple-invert) and 0EMD (lemma-simple-invert-module); prescribed finite-basis comparison and its canonical square, extracted from the inverting-ell sentence of the blueprint parent proof

proof.text: The universal property of jR gives the unique psi:A→B. Define Q:A^I→Res_psi B by taking on summand i the regular-module lift of jT(b_i). The summand formula is the regular-lift formula; naturality of multiplication and the scalar square imply Q jR^I = jT q. The finite sum of projection, jR, inclusion equals the underlying map of the biproduct-desc morphism p:R^I→Res_jR A^I.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-localization-linear-descent] to N=A^I and f=q^(-1) followed by p. It gives an A-linear g:Res_psi B→A^I with g jT = p q^(-1).

source.place: Tag 0EMD (lemma-simple-invert-module), module localization universal property, with Tag 0EMC (lemma-simple-invert) to identify arbitrary ring localizations.

proof.text: The square and q q^(-1)=1 show that g Q agrees with the identity after p. An A-linear map from A^I is determined by the images of the standard generators. Each standard A-generator is the image under p of its R-generator, because jR preserves the unit. Thus g Q=1. Apply uniqueness in [lem-sfb-localization-linear-descent] with N=Res_psi B to Q g and the identity: both restrict along jT to jT. Hence Q g=1, and Q is the required module isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0EMD (lemma-simple-invert-module), module localization universal property, with Tag 0EMC (lemma-simple-invert) to identify arbitrary ring localizations.

proof.text: The standard-generator extensionality argument also proves uniqueness of any A-linear map satisfying the square. The explicit summand formula and scalar-map uniqueness were established in the first step. Biproduct extensionality uses finite sums in the independent index universe and also covers the empty index type.
